I purchased the Qidi Tech X-Max 3d printer in August of 2019 and have had it for almost 11 months at the time of writing this review. I am not an expert in 3d printing nor claim to know what is best, this is just a review of my experience. It was my first 3D printer and did a lot of research. I was looking for something that was large format, quiet, versatile, well made, and little hassle. I read many reviews, specs, and forums along with several video reviews and how tos. It was far from the cheapest model I could have selected but I was not looking for cheap.
Packaging:
When I received the printer it was very well packed and secured in the box with ample Styrofoam around and in it. It came with 2 full 1kg rolls of filament (1 PLA and 1 ABS), tool kit, instructions, 2 removal magnetic build plates, and 2 extruders (1 high temp, and 1 normal).
Construction:
The external encloser is a nice durable ABS plastic with clear front door and clear dome top. The inside is strong metal framing and has clean routing of the wires. It is not small and is a bit heavy but feels well made.
Performance:
It took me less than 20 min from unboxing to starting my first print off of the supplied USB stick. Most of that time was the unboxing. As far as slicing software, I use the supplied Qidi Print slicer which works well for what I am using it for. Many others use Cura or S3D which is fine, but I have had no issues with Qidi Print. Leveling the bed is key so take your time and triple check it with a bed level print in between and it will save a lot of time. I rarely have to relevel the bed, usually if I change out the extruder. Since I have purchased this printer, I have purchased other cheaper popular printers and the X-Max has me spoiled. The X-max is incredibly quiet with the top cover on it and the door closed. It has had no problem doing prints ranging form .08 to .2 layer height and has creats very detailed prints. It has an Ethernet port, USB port, and Wifi. The Ethernet and USB ports are in the front which in my option is not the greatest spot. I use wifi so the ethernet port is not a big deal and I use a very stubby USB stick which took care of the concern of the USB drive sticking out to far. Wifi Connectivity works well but can be slow sending the print jobs to the printer if the files are large. I am ok with this since I am not a fan of jockeying pen drives back and forth.
Service and support:
The service, support, and Warranty from Qidi Tech is something I have never seen from any vendor on any product. On the minor issues I have had I have received an email in less then 24 hours with the answer to my question. If any part is needing replaced there is no hassle and I have received the part in just a few days with detailed instructions or videos on how to address the issue. They even went the extra mile helping with settings on a very detailed print that I was having trouble with. They went as far as taking the STL I was trying to print and running it through one of their inhouse X-Max printers and sending me the settings that best worked. This type of customer service is amazing.
Cons:
The spool holder is not the best design but works well enough. There are plenty of modifications that people have created on Thingiverse to address this. The internal spool holder for high temp materials is a good concept but is cumbersome and the filament routing is awkward but again works and is functional. I don’t use high temp filament so not an issue for me. It does have a resume feature when power is lost but there is not Filament runout sensor. Many seasoned printing enthusiasts don’t care about this but I think it would be a nice to have.
Summary:
Over all I am very happy with the X-max printer! It is a work horse, Well made, and runs darn near 24x7 for me. The Customer service is amazing and very helpful. If you are looking for a solid printer that is easy to use I would recommend the X-Max

[[VIDEOID:a23270ca4b27baef82eda4badf718e]] Wow this thing puts out some serious heat! I converted a Liquid Propane turkey fryer to natural gas for ease of use and eliminating the need to get propane refills. This burner got my 34 Qt pot boiling in less than 15 minutes. Seafood boils are now a breeze!

See pictures and video for details. If this review helped you let me know by marking as helpful thanks!

(Disclaimer -Use at own risk / for informational purposes only / follow all local code rules and regulations)

These are the parts I used to convert:
- Bayou Classic High Pressure 14 inch Cooker Model # SP10 ASIN# B000291GBQ
- 1/2 inch by 10 inch black gas pipe - Orange Big Box store SKU #1001790506
- Midline Gas Ball Valve - Model # GUHW-5IS34G ASIN# B00OQA75W6
- Harvey Gas PTFE thread seal tape - ASIN# B000FKBXCE
- 2 Stainless steel hose clamps - check your garage you probably have these laying around lol

How to:
- The Bayou Classic burner is held on by 1 screw on the bottom, unscrew it and remove the burner.
- I bent the original mounting bracket down to an L shape an inch or two lower than original to have the burner sit as close to level as possible without having to cut up the stand housing.
- Use the 2 SS hose clamps to secure the jet burner to the mounting bracket.
- The 1/2 inch black pipe can now thread into the burner - make sure to use Yellow sealant tape or pipe dope rated for gas.
- Install the Gas Ball Valve on the other end of the 1/2 inch pipe.
- My outdoor Weber natural gas grill line uses a 3/8 flare female connection which connects perfectly to the other side of the Ball gas valve.
- To light just open the ball valve less than a quarter turn and use a long neck lighter
- Once a burner is lit, you can slowly turn the gas higher so that the rest of the burners will light.

I applied this product over 3 month old, Mannington Luxury Sheet Vinyl.. When we installed the expensive, new vinyl, the surface was disappointingly course. It felt like sandpaper under my bare feet. The application was done over two days in a bathroom and kitchen. I began by scrubbing the floor with ammonia and water and a scrub brush. After thoroughly rinsing and drying, I applied 2 coats of Zep commercial sealer. Next, I applied 4 coats of the Zep Wet Look Floor Finish Gloss. I was careful to allow a minimum of 30 minutes drying time between coats. This was done over 2 days. The second day it rained and it took 1 hour in between coats for the floor to feel dry enough for the next coat. Spills dry quickly and are hard to remove, so I had to be careful to keep a rag with me and wipe up any spills immediately. All applications were done on my hands and knees with cotton rags from old t-shirts. I found that pouring the product directly onto the floor worked better than putting it in a bucket.

I have been a ARIZONA registered master heat pump technician for over 25 years.
The problem I have noticed with capacitors is that many of them are defective out of the box.
The reason I say that is I test the microfarads while the capacitor is under load which will tell me it’s exact microfarad rating. This is done by checking the amps and volts wile it is running. I use what I call the 2652 method.
The simple formula is Start Winding Amps X 2,652 ÷ Capacitor Voltage = Microfarads.
Sample: 5 amps Times 2652 divided 369 volts =35µF

This is the correct way to test a capacitor. There are meters that have capacitor testers settings on them but I never used them because they are pretty much useless unless you just wanna know what size it is. You need to put a capacitor under load to make sure it doesn’t have any leaking Through that dielectric.
This capacitor I have bought several times and it is exact to what it is rated at.
Some brands of air conditioners you will find bad capacors on every one of them when you fire them up new. I don’t wanna mention any names but one that does this the most makes air conditioners that start with the letter C and another brand with the letter B. They actually buy rejected capacitors for their units to get them cheaper so sad.
It’s very important to have a correctly size capacitor to create a third leg properly. This is basically making a third phase. If you’re capacitor is leaking electricity through the dielectric it will shorten the life of your unit. About 25% of brand new air conditioner run capacitors do not pass the test.
They can only be as far as 10% off of what they’re rated at is there any greater than that it’s best to throw them away. It’s also a good thing to change your air conditioning run capacitor at least every four years. In hotter states possibly more often.
They make a 370 V and the 440 V capacitors
I highly recommend going with the 440 V rating it will put up with more heat and will last longer.
The 440 V rating only means how much electricity it can handle. So it’s basically heavier duty than the 380V ones. Your air conditioner might be 220 V but when the compressor is running the voltage across the run cap can double that. So be warned if you’re going to test a live Ron cab you’re going to have to be extremely careful because the voltage coming off that run cap can kill you.
With that being said I recommend this brand.

Second, I purchased this to completely wire a new horn on my old truck from scratch (momentary button, this relay, inline fuse, horns, wiring - the works), and when I first did my test wire-up, it did not work (not this relay specifically, but my wire-up based on a lot of different diagrams out on the web).  Fortunately, the horns I purchased (duals from Harbor Freight for $10) had the correct wiring schematic [side note: + on the battery to an inline fuse to relay PIN30 (which gets wire-connected to relay PIN86 also); relay PIN85 to momentary switch; relay PIN87 to horns; relay PIN87a in the center unused].  All these PIN refs are clearly marked on the relay, which makes matching the colored wires on the socket easy.  [Side note2 to serious DIYselfers: you really only need the relay (or not - the horns I noted above included a relay), and not the socket (you would put your own female connectors on your own wires), but this included socket made the temporary wiring and testing much faster and easier. This printer is actually my 2nd printer. I had a 3d printer a few years ago in roughly the same price point from monoprice and had a lot of trouble dialing it in, only getting a few successful prints and then storing it away. This printer has been a breeze in comparison, pretty much out of the box there is very little needed for setup. There was a 3d printed cover over a metal piece I had to remove which was not mentioned in any guide, after that just using the application provided on the sd card and leaving things on default I was able to print things straight from thingiverse, playing around with speed, supports, and rafts. You do quickly come into some limitations of this printer and I'll list them below.

Cons:
1. Bed size: very small bed, often have to orient 3d objects in certain ways or shrink them in order to print. Still very useable but very quickly you'll design or come across something wide or long that won't fit.
2. Does not support PETG or ABS: This means you are limited to using PLA filament which is good for display things but not so much functional. PLA melts easily and has weak vertical bonds. I found this out quickly when I tried to make a glasses holder for the car and it went soft and melted in a day because it was printed in PLA.
3. The arm that holds filament is very short so you can only fit small spools of filament. On thingiverse you can find an extended arm you can print which is a workaround but I feel like it makes the filament come at an odd angle. It's easier to use small spools due to this limitation.

Lastly I wish this had a preheat function, sometimes the first print comes out a little wonky.

Despite these cons I still give this printer 5 stars because it is so easy to use, affordable, and fun and as long as you're aware of these limitations and you're looking for your first printer I think this is a great choice.

Works great...once you know how to use it properly. I used this for adding a clear coat of epoxy for tumblers. I was a total beginner when I started and learned a few things along the way that might help people like me:
1) put both bottles in the sink and fill it with warm water. Let sit for about 10 minutes. I learned the hard way that if the resin is too cold it won’t mix with the hardener properly and the result is a sticky mess. After numerous you tube videos, I found this tip and it worked great! Warming it up also helps get rid of most of the bubbles.
2) The 1:1 ratio is critical. I accidentally added a bit more hardener once(because it pours faster) and didn’t think it would make much of a difference. It does. The result never lost the tacky feel.
3) Mix for at least a minute or two. It feels like forever as your mixing, but I found the longer I mixed, the more consistent my results turned out as I mixed resin for fifteen cups in the span of two weeks. I ruined a couple cups by not mixing it enough. The results were sticky no matter how long it dried.
4) If you’re making tumblers, a “cuptisserie” motorized cup Turner is a MUST. The resin is very fluid and does not like to stay in place. Applying the resin as it’s turning was the only way possible.

I used the app from the HDMI organization to verify that the cable was certified as stated and it came back with the same information shown in the product photos. This is a legitimate certification, proving that this specific model and length of cable underwent testing to not only show that it works, but also that it did not emit harmful RF interference which could affect things like WiFi, cellular, Bluetooth, etc.

The cable is currently connecting my HD TV to my Denon A/V receiver and it's working flawlessly. It is replacing an older cable that isn't up to the current HDMI 2.1 standard. Whether using this cable will result in any functional, audible, or visible improvements seems doubtful -- until I upgrade the TV.

Bottom line: When a certified HDMI 2.1 cable is available at this price, it makes no sense to buy one that is not certified. If, using a certified cable, you encounter some problem, the seller of your TV, streaming device, DVR, A/V receiver, etc. can't get away with blaming the cable.

Most important thing. MAKE SURE THE POWER SUPPLY IS SET TO THE RIGHT VOLTAGE. If you don't know what that means, don't buy this printer. If assembling IKEA furniture intimidates you, or you are uncomfortable with working from rudimentary instructions that don't provide much detail, don't but this printer. I have worked in technical assembly/design for over 20 years, and had zero problems; but I can easily see how someone that doesn't have the same sort of experiences could struggle, especially if they aren't into troubleshooting in the event that they happen to flub a step. Not that you will need them (they are included), but if you don't own a set of hex wrenches, this printer probably isn't for you.

I set this up with my 15 year old son. If he was doing it by himself, I'm not sure it would have been put together properly; at least not on the first try. However, he was able to operate it on his own after only a few days of tutelage.

I see lots of complaints about warped beds. That hasn't been my experience. If my bed IS warped, it's so minimal that it isn't effecting my prints (I use a raft for all my prints, which may help with that). I'm also seeing a lot of complaints about bed leveling. Again, not my experience. Bed leveling isn't difficult, but it can be time consuming to get right, so be patient and seek advice on the inter-webs. If you're unsure, DON'T TRY TO GUESS YOUR WAY THROUGH THE PROCESS. I've had an less headaches leveling this printer that I ever had with my auto-leveling Monoprice Delta printer. Some of the leveling complaints I'm reading lead me to believe that some people didn't setup the z-axis switch at the right height; so make doubly sure you have it set how the instructions state.

As for print quality; I don't know what one would expect from a printer at this price point, but I'm happy with the quality for what I paid.

I wouldn't recommend this printer for anyone with zero experience with 3D printing, zero experience with this sort of machinery, or who just isn't into assembling their own stuff. However, if you ARE a complete noob to printing, BUT have experience with similar equipment and software, or have 3d printing experience/knowledge, like building stuff, but have never owned a printer; I would give this a recommendation.

[UPDATE on 1/1/23: our total electricity consumption in 2022 dropped even further to just 5,500 kWh (1,600 of which was for HVAC) for the year. We have HALVED our electricity consumption. Huge savings. This thermal imager continues to operate beautifully. We lend it to friends & family so they can do their own diagnostics to save energy.]

We first used our Klein Tools TI250 Rechargeable Thermal Imager to identify where our home’s protective envelop was weak – places where we were losing heat / allowing cold air inside in the winter and losing cool air / allowing heat inside in the summer. The imager revealed problem areas we had suspected, e.g., around windows and doors – areas where we needed to improve weatherstripping. But above all they highlighted an extremely acute problem we hadn’t focused on, namely the 7 recessed lights in our kitchen. In summer, and with those lights off, the thermal imager showed the lights as 7 ultra-bright, fiercely orange circles, though the ceiling all around (under thick insulation) was deep, cool blue. I have been using this thread sealer for over 22 years and have assembled 10's of thousands of NPT threaded joints with it. Rarely will I get a leak. I have used this alone and also with PTFE tape. The reason for the tape and the sealer used together is that most of my NPT joints are plastic Polypropylene/PVC/CPVC and Kynar. Sometimes plastic NPT joints/threads can be a little sloppy from manufacturer to manufacturer so using both in this scenario fills in the larger gaps and creates a leak free joint pretty much every time.  In my experience it will NOT harden rock hard but will set up and remain pliable pretty much indefinitely . Once set up you can touch it and it will not want to stick back on you. This thread sealer does not have the little bits of PTFE in it like some of the other brands of thread sealer.  The color of this stuff is a bluish green and it has an exceptionally smooth thick consistency. If properly applied it will not run.  If you let it sit in the can for extended periods you will need to mix it with the included in-can brush before use. If I get it on my skin I use a strong alcohol like isopropyl or others to clean it off. The only annoyance I find with it is the rubber seal in the cap sometimes sticks to the rim of the can and comes out of the cap upon opening. I remedy this by putting a little bit of adhesive in between the inside of the metal cap and then put the rubber seal back in. I have tried other thread sealers but this is my go to product. Excellent! Hope it helps. Cheers!

I got perplexed installing a water hammer arrestor. The water hammer arrestor was labeled "1/4" O.D." But its male fittings were 1/4" inside diameter (I.D.). I couldn't understand why this 1/4" I.D. female coupler slid over the male fittings. The male fittings were 0.43" and this female couple is 0.455". After spending way too much time searching on the Internet I put on my mask and went to Home Depot. The plumbing aisle employee told me that the water hammer arrestor had a compression fitting. I went home and found a YouTube video explaining how to connect compression fittings. Twenty minutes later I'd installed my water hammer arrestor, with no extra parts. So I never used this brass coupler but it looks nice. :-)

My pipe is 0.25" inside diameter and the outside diameter of the male threads are 0.43". This coupling has an inside diameter of the female threads of 0.44". Okay, so I used this to attach 2 Ikea carpets together to make a bigger one! Once you unwrap the tape,
1: attach to back side of carpet (make sure it is aligned)
2: use a rag that is wet, (not soaked but wet) and place it over the brown part of the tape.

THE YELLOW SIDE SHOULD BE FACING AND TOUCHING THE CARPET

3: use a iron, any kind will do as long as you lower the setting I used heat 4 from a standard Walmart iron. And going ON TOP of the rag go over it multiple times, about 30-40 seconds to make sure it melts together!

Important note: I found that using moisture on a rag is best, it was quicker and did not smell like burning tire when used.

4: once the entire section you want is dried you can take off the paper surrounding the yellow. You can leave it on I found out that it did not effect the durability of the adhesive!

I'm running a direct drive mod on my Ender 3 and a BMG dual gear clone. With this setup, I cut a 3mm piece of bowden tube to put inside the extruder to snug it up against the hotend and mounted this hotend directly into the BMG extruder. Filament changes are easy, the screw in thermistor is a game changer (especially since it comes with a connector and extension, so next time I need to change it I don't have to pull it all the way out of the mainboard... Though, since it's not a flimsy piece of glass, will I need to change it as often anyway?)

Honestly it's been printing like a dream with PLA so far (I am replacing a Microswiss hotend that I managed to bend several degrees out of square when I was moving).

Current PLA direct drive settings:
Hotend: 192C
Bed: 60C
Retraction: 1.2mm@20mm/s
Nozzle: 0.4mm (though I tend to prefer 0.5 or 0.6 -- I'm keeping the stock nozzle on this for now out of convenience)

Printer: Ender 3
Printer Firmware: Klipper (with a Raspberry Pi 2B running Klipper/Fluidd)
Bed: Creality glass bed (smooth side up)
Direct drive mount: Printermods MDD 1.3
Extruder: BMG clone

UPDATE: My heat break broke while I was tightening everything down to stop a leaking nozzle. GCR sent me a replacement right away. Great customer service.

I had been looking at 3 D printers for a while and when I spotted one that looked promising and even if it had been given a four star rating, reading the reviews made me skeptical. This one had eleven five star reviews when I decided to take the plunge, and here is one more. I had no prior experience with 3 D printing, I understood the process but never saw one in real life operation, this little machine makes learning easy. The machine is very easy to use once you have it set up, although I did find a couple of things I did not like about the design.
First the Z axis drive was too close to the column, the lead screw was not parallel to the column. The machine worked but this condition put some strain on the stepper when the gantry was in the lowest position, I added a .032" brass shim between the motor mount and the column and this almost brought the two parts parallel for the length of the screw.
Second, the bracket that mounts the guide wheel and lead screw nut to the gantry can not be adjusted one the machine is assembled. I was unable to level the table initially because gantry was out of square with the columns, I could square up the gantry but there was no way to tighten the screws to try to hold it in that position. I used a machinist square to get the gantry aligned with column on the drive side and then drilled two 1/8" holes through the gantry and wheel mount and used SS dowels to secure the alignment of the two pieces.
Lastly, even after resolving the gantry problem the spring on one corner of the bed was not very compressed compared to the other springs after leveling the bed, so I added a couple of washers under the spring, seems to have done the trick.
It took four tries to get the sample doggy printed using Hatchbox PLA, first one warped after about 1/8" of buildup using the programed bed and nozzle temps, lowered them both. Second and third wouldn't stick to the bed, too much clearance between the nozzle and bed, forth time was the charm with nozzle at 195 C and the bed at 35 C.
I am using Cura for my slicer and have a old version of Solid Works that I have used for 3 D modeling. I am going to try Tinkercad next.
Despite the problems I encountered, for the price and ease of use I still feel the machine deserves *****

Tourniquets are an item you have with you and hope that you never have to use them. So this review is based on my experience in the field, rather that having used this item in a real emergency.

I would rate these as a pretty good tourniquet. I know that comfort is not the goal of a tourniquet, but these were not all that uncomfortable. The windlass tightened up quickly and was able to cut off the pulse in my leg adequately. The hardware is strong enough that I did not feel like anything would break when the pressure was applied. The securing strap for the windlass is also white and able to be written on to write a time when the tourniquet was placed. The windlass did not create any unnecessary pinch points that would cause undue damage or discomfort. Overall these are pretty good tourniquets.

The one thing that I did not like was the packaging. They come in a sealed plastic bag with instructions. So the only way I can inspect the item for defects before placing it in service is to remove it from the bag. Then, to keep the tourniquet and the instructions together, I have to place them in another resealable bag. This one simple thing would make a world of difference in being able to use these more effectively in the field.
These tourniquets will be placed in my medical bag for Search and Rescue.

I am using the temp stick in a cabin located on a mountain where it gets very very cold. I did a lot of research comparing remote temperature monitors before buying Temp Stick. I ran the Temp Stick all summer and fall to determine its reliability and alert capability. The sensor is spot on, same read out as the temperature on the thermostat.

I've ordered a second Temp Stick; in addition, I am using lithium batteries. Call it overkill, but I want to know if the temperature in the cabin begins to drop! I don't want/need a repeat of last winter.

Initially, I had a few questions setting up the temp stick. My questions were answered promptly, professionally, and thoroughly by tech support. I called again recently; Josh in tech support demonstrated just how important customer service is with this company.

Temp Stick is providing the peace of mind I need in anticipation of another very cold, freezing winter.

I got these casters to replace a set I had on my custom built kayak stand. It holds two full size 13 foot kayaks with loads of fishing gear. The old wheels were too small. They wouldn't swivel easy, so it was hard to move around. They also wouldn't go over the bump in the concrete to go in and out of my garage.

Enter these wheels. They're similar load capacity, but larger diameter than what I had. I was pleasantly surprised that I was able to remove the old casters, and bolt these right on. The mounting plate seems fairly universal, so it should work in most applications where you're replacing another set of wheels.

These wheels have a hard poly/rubber type material. I'm not dragging the thing down the road behind my truck, but going in and out of the garage, they're taking no wear at all. My kayak cart is probably 3-400lbs or so with the kayaks on board, but it's big and awkward with two big kayaks on it. Never mind all the junk piled on the kayaks, you'll see the cart in the pictures.

The garage has about a 3/4" lip where the driveway is lower, and pushing the cart in with the old wheels was impossible. You had to lift the cart up over the bump. These wheels roll right over it like it's not even there. I was bracing to ram full speed ahead over that hump, and it slid by like it was nothing. My back is happy about that.

The lock on these wheels is FIRM. It's a solid thunk when it locks in, and takes a good tug to pop up. It's not difficult, it's just sturdy and reliable. The cart won't roll if even just one wheel is locked.

I can push the kayak cart sideway with ease, despite whatever direction the wheels are facing. This used to be a major pain in the back trying it with the old wheels. These allow 100% freedom of movement. It just glides wherever I want it.

Finally price. The price of these things is great. Some wheels can be this much for ONE wheel! I wouldn't hesitate to recommend these. These are smooth rolling, strong locking sturdy well made wheels. I would definitely recommend them and wouldn't hesitate to acquire another set in the future.

This is one of the best floor scrubbers I’ve ever used. My house is entirely hardwood floors and I have four dogs living at home. On rainy days, it’s impossible to keep the floors clean from dried dirt. This scrubber has been a life saver for getting rid of dirt that gets caught in between the cracks or indents.

Essentially, I will mop or wipe the floors with warm water and soap first. I don’t necessarily think the scrubber is great for cleaning giant areas quickly. I bust out the scrubber so that I can clean out the small indents between the wood sections where dirt usually gets left behind after mopping.

The scrubber is incredibly strong even on the first setting. I can’t imagine using the second setting unless it’s something very heavy duty stuck on your ground. The scrubber comes with four different heads that was made up of very sturdy plastic hairs. The whole body is made up of three parts that can be easily assembled and dissembled. The instruction pamphlet is very straight forward with illustrations to help assemble. One section also extends about an extra 10 inches which is great if you’re taller. It keeps from straining your back!

The scrubber also comes with a hook where you can hang it across any bar or to the wall for easy storage and access. Lastly, the scrubber head can be adjusted to be completely 180 degrees, 140 degrees, or 90 degrees. That’s extremely useful based on what kind of area you are trying to clean. It’s so ergonomic!! I highly recommend the scrubber for anyone looking for one!
